clue.text: Workman's top ass to raise extremes of excitement!

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
to jack something up is to raise it

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here taken from excitement

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a labourer whose shirt-off antics drive excitement to new heights.
explanation.walkthrough: A DONKEY JACKET is the heavy short coat with a shoulder patch traditionally worn by British manual workers.
explanation.definitionFit: This thick wool coat is the classic outer garment of a British labourer, so a workman's top.

clue.text: Dislikes of French when facing exams

parts.note: de is French for of
exams are tests

explanation.surface: Someone loathes the French section of their exam timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to dislike intensely; both are third-person verbs here.

clue.text: Mug from hotel in New York

indicators.note: the word in tells us the lodging sits inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: A stolen coffee mug turns up at a New York hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Mug is slang for a fool or dupe, the same as a simpleton.

clue.text: Always consort with Eastern bird on top

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top puts the first pieces above the partner in the column

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
to consort with is to ally oneself

explanation.surface: Someone forever keeps company with an oriental bird perched up high.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs meaning forever, at all times without end.

clue.text: Can be sickly after onset of jaundice

indicators.note: after places the illness word behind the opening letter
the onset of a word is its opening letter, taken from jaundice

parts.note: to ail is to be sickly

explanation.surface: A tin may make you feel ill once yellow skin appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Can is slang for prison, a synonym used chiefly in American English.

indicators.note: wiggles means these letters squirm into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sweet, unusual animal is seen wriggling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: A being is any living creature, one more noun for a living thing.

parts.note: the former French president would name his boredom with a French word, which English has borrowed whole

explanation.surface: A former French president feels jaded.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicolas Sarkozy was President of France, so the question mark hints that the answer is a French word for boredom also used in English.
explanation.definitionFit: This borrowed French term names listless weariness or boredom.

clue.text: Head of foreign state English already settled

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of foreign

parts.note: Oregon is a US state

explanation.surface: A foreign leader declares that matters with the English are already decided.
explanation.definitionFit: A foregone conclusion is one decided in advance, so settled beforehand.

clue.text: Novel hero half lost on middle of Yorkshire moors

indicators.note: half lost means the second half of the name is dropped

parts.note: Heathcliff is the hero of Emily Bronte's novel Wuthering Heights

indicators.note: the middle of Yorkshire is its central letter

explanation.surface: A fictional hero, half-ruined, wanders the Yorkshire moors.
explanation.walkthrough: Wuthering Heights is set on the Yorkshire moors, which makes the surface apt; dropping the last five of the hero's ten letters leaves HEATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaths and moors are both open uncultivated upland covered in heather.

clue.text: Fork bit eating bad blood orange

indicators.note: eating means the prong word swallows the other piece

parts.note: a tine is one prong of a fork
bad blood is anger or hostility

explanation.surface: A prong of a fork digs into a blood orange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blood orange' looks like one phrase, but 'bad blood' gives ANGER and 'orange' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small loose-skinned citrus fruit, a kind of orange.

clue.text: Beak accepts old form of execution

indicators.note: accepts means the nose word takes the other letter inside it

parts.note: beak is slang for nose

explanation.surface: A magistrate agrees to an outdated method of capital punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Beak is also British slang for a magistrate, which the surface exploits.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging with a rope loop is a method of execution.

definitions.meaning: a platitude is a trite remark or proverb

explanation.definitionFit: Spouting words is speaking them, and a trite adage is a common proverb or byword.

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of Spartacus

parts.note: a trident is a three-pronged spear

explanation.surface: The gladiator Spartacus stabs with his spear.
explanation.walkthrough: Spartacus was a gladiator, and the trident was a gladiator's weapon, so the picture fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice is harsh and piercing to the ear.

indicators.note: opening takes the first letter of Star

parts.note: an ample figure is a busty one

explanation.surface: A celebrity debut featuring a curvaceous model.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample is a specimen or example, as a model is a representative example.

clue.text: Under sea, flog, keeping one in hold

indicators.note: in a down clue the beating word goes under the sea word

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the sea

indicators.note: keeping means the beating word holds the numeral inside

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to flog them
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Below decks, a sailor is flogged while another is kept in the ship's hold.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a position is to hold it, keeping it unchanged.

clue.text: Revered devout taking religious education by Catholic

indicators.note: taking means the devout word takes the others inside

parts.note: devout means pious

indicators.note: by places the Catholic letter beside the subject

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: A devout pupil studies religion with a Catholic teacher and is held in reverence.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the British school subject Religious Education.
explanation.definitionFit: Something precious is cherished and held dear, as a revered thing is.

parts.note: a daily is a cleaning lady, also called a char
to show a role is to act it
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A newspaper puts on a show about the Queen's personality.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily, or char, is British for a cleaning woman who comes in each day; 'Daily' looks like a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Character is one's personality, the combination of traits that make a person.

parts.note: Kansas is a US state

explanation.surface: Is this one state? Yes, and a proper mess of a state!
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: the answer is one particular state.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkansas is one of the fifty US states, an instance of a state.

parts.note: a junk is a Chinese sailing boat, and a shop is a workshop, so a junk shop is where boats are built

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase looks like a second-hand store, but the vessel sense of junk and workshop sense of shop give a place where ships are made.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipyard is a workshop where vessels, junks included, are built and repaired.

indicators.note: on board places the group inside the ship's abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a wing is a faction of a party

explanation.surface: A rebel group is hanged aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Swings and hangs are both verbs for dangling or suspending from a point.

parts.note: worries are cares

explanation.surface: Someone frets about their little pet.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet an animal is to stroke it fondly, a gentle caress.

clue.text: Sweetheart in delicate embrace shows dexterity

indicators.note: embrace means the slender word hugs the letter inside

parts.note: slight means delicate or slender

indicators.note: the heart of Sweet is its central letter

explanation.surface: A loving couple hugs gently, showing nimble skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' splits into 'Sweet' plus 'heart', the middle letter of SWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight means deftness of hand, as in sleight of hand.

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged otherwise

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suggestion of time travel.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a period of time between events.

indicators.note: reveals means the letters are exposed within the run of words

explanation.surface: A prison leak exposes stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir is British slang for prison, which the surface uses.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search and plunder it, a synonym for loot.

definitions.meaning: unsophisticated means socially awkward or clumsy

explanation.definitionFit: The English adjective means socially awkward, and in French it is simply the word for left.

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A Tory MP faces a hard slog.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb is an ascent, and figuratively a hard uphill effort.

clue.text: Couple starts to play around in relationship

indicators.note: starts to takes the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Partners begin fooling around within a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two together, the same as a couple.

clue.text: Figure United's lost badly creating despair

indicators.note: badly means the remaining letters are jumbled
lost means the club letter is dropped

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United

explanation.surface: A football figure whose club lost heavily is in despair.
explanation.walkthrough: FIGURE without U leaves FIGRE, which 'badly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief is deep sorrow, akin to despair.

indicators.note: taking means the bird word takes the letter inside

parts.note: a starling is a bird

explanation.surface: A marvellous bird takes its time.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling means astonishing, close to fantastic in its sense of amazing.

indicators.note: stew as a verb means to cook slowly, churning the letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wife cooks an awful stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'stew' does the stirring. Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a savoury dish of melted cheese on toast.
